nodes.action_phrase: whisk eggs with salt and pepper
source_spans: Whisk together eggs, milk, salt and pepper.
Whisk 1/4 teaspoon kosher salt and a few grinds of black pepper into the eggs.
Melt butter over medium heat (Note 1), then pour egg in.

Wait 5 seconds, then start leisurely pushing the rubber spatula back and forth in long strokes, and all around the skillet edges, to push the set egg out of the way and let raw egg run onto the skillet to cook. After 30 seconds or so, start adding some folding action too.

source_spans: Add 1 teaspoon unsalted butter and let it begin to melt
Pour the eggs into the pan. The eggs will spread out in a thin layer — that's fine.

Stir the eggs occasionally with a spatula. At first the eggs will be very liquidy; then you'll notice large, opaque curds starting to form. Eventually, the eggs will no longer run in to fill the gaps when you stir. Frequent stirring will give you smaller curds; stirring less frequently will give you larger, irregular curds. Continue cooking until the eggs are as soft or as firm as you like them, about 10 to 15 minutes.
